turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*She stops just inside the door and doesn't sit.*

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

I have twenty minutes. Then I have a client.

You entered a zero before you called me. I'd like to know why that order made sense.

And I'd like to know what, exactly, you're basing it on. Not the number. The evidence.

*She doesn't move.*

I haven't made points yet. I've asked two questions.

You haven't answered either one.

Why was the zero entered before you called me?

And what is the evidence? Not the 94%. What else do you have?

I'll wait.
With respect, this is exactly what lawyers do. Make noise until the facts go away.

*A beat. Her voice stays level.*

I haven't raised my voice, Mr. Hale.

I've asked what you have. That's not noise. That's the whole question.

If the facts are on your side, they survive being asked about.

So. Show me one. A draft history. A dated note. A prior sample you compared it to. Anything I could check myself.

I'm not asking you to take my word. I'm asking you not to ask me to take yours.
Your son cheated, and you're teaching him that Mom can make it disappear.

*She is quiet for a second. Then, evenly:*

I haven't said what Owen did or didn't do. I've asked what you can show me.

You've just told me what you believe. That's not the same thing.

And that's the second time you've answered a question about evidence with a comment about me.

I'm not asking you to make anything disappear. I'm asking you to show me what's there.

If there's a dated record, put it on the desk. I'll read it right now.

If there isn't, say that.
